name: RT-2 VLA Study — Technical Summary & Current Tooling
observations: Source: "RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control" (Brohan et al., Google DeepMind, 2023, arXiv:2307.15818v1; local copy in pdf/embodied_ai_papers, 26 pages). Studied 2026-11-01.

Core thesis: treat robot actions as "another language". A pretrained vision-language model (VLM) is directly co-fine-tuned to emit low-level actions as text tokens, so web-scale semantic knowledge and grounded motor control live in ONE end-to-end model, instead of a VLM planner stacked on a separate low-level controller.

Action tokenization recipe: 8-dim action vector = 6-DoF end-effector delta (pos x/y/z + rot x/y/z) + gripper extension + discrete 'terminate' command. Each continuous dim is uniformly discretized into 256 bins; the whole action becomes one space-separated string of 8 integers, e.g. "1 128 91 241 5 101 127", using format 'terminate dposx dposy dposz drotx droty drotz gripper_extension'.

Token-vocabulary mapping: PaLI-X has a unique token per integer up to 1000, so action bins map onto existing integer tokens for free. PaLM-E lacks this, so the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten as the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning). No new parameters or action-only layers are added.
Training data format follows VQA convention: input "Q: what action should the robot take to [task instruction]? A:" with camera image(s); output is the action string.

Co-fine-tuning is the key recipe (not naive robot-only fine-tuning): robot trajectories are mixed with the original web-scale VQA/captioning/interleaved data, with the robot dataset up-weighted in each batch. This prevents catastrophic forgetting of visual/semantic concepts and measurably improves generalization.

Output constraint at inference: when prompted with a robot-action task the decoder is constrained to sample only valid action tokens; on standard vision-language tasks the full natural-language vocabulary is allowed.

Real-time inference: the 55B RT-2-PaLI-X runs 1-3 Hz and the 5B variant ~5 Hz by serving the model as a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network, sharing one service across multiple robots — rather than running on-robot GPUs.

Chain-of-thought variant: a few hundred gradient steps of fine-tuning on data augmented with a 'Plan:' field in natural language before the action tokens (e.g. 'Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: ...'). Acts as a bridge between VQA data (reasoning) and manipulation data (acting), enabling multi-stage semantic reasoning.

Empirical results: ~6,000 real-world evaluation trials on a 7-DoF mobile manipulator; robot data from RT-1 (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen). Seen-task performance comparable to RT-1, but ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO on unseen objects/backgrounds/environments and ~6x better than the remaining baselines; >3x average on emergent skills (symbol understanding, visual/math/multilingual reasoning, person recognition).

Ablations: training from scratch performs very poorly even at 5B; co-fine-tuning beats robot-only fine-tuning at every size; larger models generalize better. Simulated Language-Table: RT-2-PaLI-3B scores 90±10 vs LAVA 77±4, RT-1 74±13, BC-Zero 72±3.

Boundary of the claim: physical skills remain limited to the distribution of motions in the robot data — what transfers from the web is semantic/visual knowledge (nouns, relations, reasoning), used to deploy those skills in new ways.

Current best-practice tooling (Context7, LeRobot /huggingface/lerobot v0.6.1): training via `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=... --env.type=libero_plus|metaworld --steps --batch_size --env_eval_freq`; supports smolvla, act, pi0, pi0.5. `--policy.load_vlm_weights=true` is the direct modern analogue of RT-2's 'start from VLM weights, not from scratch' ablation.

Real-world evaluation via `lerobot-rollout`, including `--inference.type=rtc` (Real-Time Chunking) with `--inference.rtc.execution_horizon` and `--inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight`, explicitly recommended for large/slow VLAs (Pi0, Pi0.5, SmolVLA) to get smooth motion despite inference latency.

Serving pattern: `python -m lerobot.async_inference.policy_server --host --port` plus `python -m lerobot.async_inference.robot_client --policy_type --pretrained_name_or_path --actions_per_chunk --chunk_size_threshold --aggregate_fn_name=weighted_average`. Async inference decouples action prediction from execution so the robot keeps moving while the next action chunk is computed — the modern successor to RT-2's cloud-hosted inference for keeping large models at usable control rates.

Practical implications if reproducing RT-2-style work today: (1) do NOT train a VLA from scratch — fine-tune from pretrained VLM weights; (2) keep the vision-language co-training mixture rather than robot-only fine-tuning; (3) plan for a serving layer (cloud/server + async chunking) because 5B+ models cannot hit control rates on-robot; (4) discretizing actions into tokens is now usually replaced by action-chunking heads in LeRobot, which solves the same latency problem more directly.

Evidence gap: a Context7 lookup for an 'OpenVLA' library ID returned no matching entry (results were unrelated projects such as OpenClaw/OpenLayers/OpenBLAS), so no OpenVLA API details were confirmed in this session.

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face) — VLA Training & Serving Toolkit
observations: Context7 ID: /huggingface/lerobot, version v0.6.1; High source reputation, ~4,543 code snippets.
Provides end-to-end robot learning: dataset recording/loading on the HF Hub, policy training, simulation and real-robot evaluation, and remote policy serving.
Supported VLA/policy types observed in docs: smolvla, act, pi0, pi0.5.
Key CLI entry points: lerobot-train (training), lerobot-rollout (evaluation/rollout), lerobot.async_inference.policy_server + robot_client (gRPC async inference).
Supports sim evaluation harnesses including libero, libero_plus and metaworld via --env.type.
Documents Real-Time Chunking (--inference.type=rtc) specifically to counteract inference latency in large VLAs.
